recentItems.title: Education crisis in Lebanon: Students return to school as Israeli attacks continue
recentItems.description:
Hundreds of thousands of people have returned to their homes in southern Lebanon after a ceasefire was agreed in June. But many more remain displaced because of Israel’s occupation and ongoing strikes. With the school year about to start, the education minister says Beirut is determined to ensure every child has a seat in a classroom. 

Al Jazeera’s Zeina Khodr reports from Nabatieh in Lebanon.

recentItems.title: El Nino's effect on Sudan: Delayed rains lead to a difficult harvest season
recentItems.description:
Sudan’s farmers are entering another difficult agricultural season as an El Nino weather pattern grows stronger. The World Meteorological Organization says the phenomenon is expected to affect rainfall patterns across parts of the region in the coming months.

In North Kordofan, Al Migdad Al-ruhaid reports on what delayed rains and changing weather patterns could mean for communities already under severe pressure.

recentItems.title: Israeli raids on occupied West Bank: Two Palestinians killed in al-Mughayyir village
recentItems.description:
Israeli forces have killed two Palestinians during a raid on al-Mughayyir village, east of Ramallah. Witnesses say snipers were positioned on rooftops during the raid. The village has faced repeated settler attacks in recent months. The UN identifies the area as one of the worst affected by settler violence.

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim joins live from al-Mughayyir in the occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Former campaign chair: Trump ‘cares about Trump the most’
recentItems.description:
Former Trump campaign chair Rob Arlett tells Al Jazeera’s ‘This is America’ that US President Trump is focused on protecting both the Republican Party and himself. Arlett argues Trump’s personal brand and ability to motivate voters remains central to the GOP’s midterm strategy.

recentItems.title: Andy Burnham’s first PMQs: Badenoch challenges Labour leader on debt and defence
recentItems.description:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has faced his first Prime Minister’s Questions in Parliament, with the session dominated by questions over government spending, national debt and defence.

Opposition Leader Kemi Badenoch challenged Burnham over his government’s fiscal plans, calling for greater clarity on debt reduction and defence spending.

Burnham defended his government’s approach, stressing fiscal responsibility and the need to reduce debt.

Outside Westminster, climate activists from Just Stop Oil staged a protest against North Sea oil drilling. Several people were arrested, according to the report.

Al Jazeera's Milena Veselinovic reports
